turns.user: Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter disruption?

answer.answer:
Of the 7 Midwest hubs, Minneapolis is the most exposed to winter disruption by a wide margin: winter sub-score 75.9, driven by 34.6 observed winter-disruption days/yr (rank 1 across the whole portfolio on observed days; rule: snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C) plus FEMA NRI winter weather 47.7 / ice storm 32.0.

Next are Detroit (43.5) and Chicago (35.9). Detroit sees fewer observed days (10.4/yr, portfolio rank 5) but carries the heavier FEMA NRI long-term winter signal of the group shown here (63.8, with WNTW 77.1 and ISTM 50.4); Chicago has slightly more observed days (11.8/yr, rank 4) but a lower NRI long-term score (38.6).

The remaining four cluster closely: Kansas City 30.5 (8.2 days/yr), Indianapolis 27.7 (7.0), St. Louis 26.7 (5.2) and Columbus 26.3 (6.2 days/yr, tied with Newark on observed days). For resilience investment, Minneapolis is the clear winter priority, with Detroit and Chicago second-tier — note their composite risk is driven partly by other hazards (flood in Chicago and St. Louis, severe storm in Kansas City).
reasoning: Ranked all 7 Midwest hubs by the winter hazard sub-score.
Minneapolis leads on both components: highest observed winter-disruption days/yr in the portfolio (34.6) and solid FEMA NRI winter/ice-storm percentiles.
Detroit ranks above Chicago despite fewer observed days because its FEMA NRI long-term winter score is higher (63.8 vs 38.6).
Lower four hubs differ by only ~4 points, so the ordering among them is not a meaningful separation.
assumptions: Scores are 0-100 and relative to this 22-hub portfolio; tiers are prioritization bands, not probabilities.
Observed disruption days come from point-location daily history at each hub, not county-wide conditions.
Winter sub-score blends observed frequency with FEMA NRI long-term percentiles.
answer.confidence_reason: Winter ranking comes directly from the deterministic scoring engine, though the lower four hubs are closely bunched.

answer.answer:
Winter is a minor hazard across the South — all 7 Southern hubs score well below the Midwest leaders (Minneapolis 75.9, Detroit 43.5).

Ranking by winter sub-score: Memphis 18.0 (2.0 disruption days/yr, portfolio rank 14; NRI long-term 36.3, WNTW 31.5 / ISTM 41.1), Charlotte 17.4 (0.4 days/yr; NRI 41.8, ISTM 52.3), Dallas 15.3 (1.2 days/yr; NRI 33.0), Atlanta 14.6 (0.4 days/yr), Houston 13.8 (0.4 days/yr), New Orleans 11.6 (0.2 days/yr) and Miami 0.0 (no observed winter-disruption days and NRI winter weather 0.0). Charlotte, Atlanta and Houston are tied on observed days (0.4/yr, rank 16); their ordering comes from the FEMA NRI long-term component. Disruption days use the rule: snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C.

Practically, winter is not the reason to invest in any Southern hub: top drivers are flood and hurricane almost everywhere — Houston (flood 92.8, hurricane 72.0, composite 41.2, High), New Orleans (hurricane 90.5, flood 81.5, composite 46.7, High), Miami (hurricane 92.7), Dallas (flood 69.3, severe storm 64.9). Memphis and Charlotte lead on winter but both sit in the Low composite tier (27.0 and 28.8).
reasoning: Ranked the 7 Southern hubs by the winter hazard sub-score, mirroring the Midwest question.
Observed winter-disruption days are near zero across the South (0.0-2.0/yr), so the winter sub-scores are driven largely by FEMA NRI winter weather and ice storm percentiles.
Checked each hub's top drivers to flag that flood and hurricane, not winter, dominate Southern composite scores.

Observed days come from point-location daily history at each hub over the tool's history window.
Rare hard-freeze events (e.g. Gulf Coast ice storms) are poorly captured by short observed windows.

turns.user: Why is the top one there so exposed?

answer.answer:
Taking "the top one" as Memphis — the leader of the Southern winter ranking — it's worth correcting the premise: Memphis isn't especially exposed. Its winter score is 18.0 and its composite is 27.0, which sits in the Low tier at rank 13 of 22 hubs. It tops the South on winter only because Southern winter scores are all small.

What the winter score is made of: 2.0 observed winter-disruption days/yr over 2021-2025 (snowfall >= 2.5 cm OR min temp <= -18.0 C), which normalizes to 5.8 and ranks 14th in the portfolio, blended 60/40 with a FEMA NRI long-term score of 36.3 (winter weather 31.5, ice storm 41.1 — Memphis's relatively notable ice-storm exposure is what lifts it above the other Southern hubs). Winter carries the largest composite weight (0.25) but contributes only 4.5 of Memphis's 27.0 points.

What actually drives Memphis: flood is the largest contributor at 10.4 points (score 51.8 — 2.4 heavy-rain days/yr >= 50 mm, portfolio rank 5 tied with Los Angeles, plus NRI inland flood 40.3), then severe storm at 7.7 points (score 38.3, NRI tornado percentile 87.7, hail 3.8, strong wind 29.1, 3.6 gust days/yr >= 70 km/h). Hurricane adds 3.9 and heat just 0.5. Supporting evidence: since 2000 Memphis has had 14 severe-storm, 2 winter-storm and 2 severe-ice-storm federal major-disaster declarations.

If you meant the most exposed Southern hub overall rather than on winter, that's New Orleans (composite 46.7, High) on hurricane and flood — happy to break that one down.
reasoning: Resolved "the top one there" to Memphis, top of the Southern winter ranking from the previous turn.
Checked Memphis's full breakdown: winter 18.0, composite 27.0, Low tier, rank 13/22 — so the 'so exposed' premise doesn't hold.
Decomposed the winter score into its 60% observed-frequency half (2.0 days/yr, normalized 5.8) and 40% FEMA NRI half (36.3, ice storm 41.1), which is what edges it past other Southern hubs.
Used contributions_ranked to show flood (10.4 pts) and severe storm (7.7 pts) are the real drivers, corroborated by 14 severe-storm DR declarations.
assumptions: Interpreted the question as about Memphis (top of the winter list just given), not the top composite hub in the South.
Observed frequency averages full calendar years 2021-2025 only; rare events are under-sampled, which is why NRI percentiles are blended in.
Scores are relative to this 22-hub portfolio; tiers are prioritization bands, not probabilities. Each hub is a single point in ERA5 (~25 km grid); NRI percentiles describe the county.
answer.confidence_reason: The breakdown comes straight from the scoring engine, though the 5-year observed window makes the 2.0 winter days/yr figure statistically thin.
